evidence.trl_pathway: All three technologies start at TRL 1 and must reach deployment-ready status within 2-4 years, which is highly aggressive; TRL 1 to market-ready in 2 years (TECH-001) is particularly unrealistic given that TRL 1 represents basic principles only and typical battery material development cycles require 5-8 years from TRL 1 to commercialization.
evidence.strategic_fidelity: The selection of three TRL-1 technologies with high uncertainty scores (5.0) and long development horizons strongly embodies a 기술선도 strategy, emphasizing exploratory R&D and technology preemption; strategic fit scores are moderate (3-4), slightly diluting the purity of the technology leadership positioning.
evidence.competitive_awareness: There is no visible evidence in the roadmap of competitor positioning, technology gap analysis, or differentiation rationale; technology selections appear driven by market opportunity scores rather than competitive landscape intelligence or timing advantages relative to rivals.
evidence.market_timing: For 기술선도, completing 1-2 years before the market boom is ideal, and all three technologies complete approximately 0.75-1.0 year after their respective boom windows, which is suboptimal but not severely misaligned; the mean timing error of 0.92 years represents a modest overshoot rather than systematic preemptive positioning.
evidence.patent_market_convergence: All three selected technologies have high market opportunity scores (4-5), and their inclusion in a battery materials domain suggests awareness of active patent landscapes, but there is no explicit evidence of deliberate convergence-zone targeting or differentiation between patent-heavy and market-driven signals.

strengths: Strong alignment with 기술선도 strategy through consistent selection of TRL-1 technologies with high uncertainty and long development horizons
Budget is fully utilized with zero violations and no dependency conflicts, indicating disciplined resource allocation
weaknesses: TRL 1 starting points combined with 2-4 year completion targets are fundamentally unrealistic for battery material development, undermining roadmap credibility
All technologies complete after their respective market boom windows, missing the preemptive positioning advantage that defines technology leadership strategy
missing_technologies: Solid-state electrolyte materials (higher TRL bridge technology to de-risk TRL-1 portfolio)
Lithium manganese-rich (LMR) or LNMO spinel cathode materials as mid-TRL complement
Dry electrode coating process technology to support cathode material commercialization pathway
investment_issues: Executability scores of 1.0 across all technologies signal near-impossible implementation risk yet investment tiers remain Strategic/High/Medium — there is a disconnect between execution feasibility and investment commitment
Concentrating the entire budget on three TRL-1 technologies with maximum uncertainty (5.0) creates extreme portfolio risk with no hedge from higher-TRL near-term technologies
Medium tier assignment to Silicon-Based Negative Electrode Materials despite its market opportunity score of 5.0 (highest in portfolio) appears misaligned with value maximization
timing_issues: High-Nickel Polycrystalline Cathode Materials completes Q1 2028 but boom is Q2 2027, arriving 0.75 years late — misses preemption window for technology leadership
LiFSI Recovery & Synthesis completes Q1 2029 vs boom Q1 2028, arriving 1 full year late — opportunity for first-mover advantage lost
Silicon-Based Negative Electrode Materials completes Q1 2030 vs boom Q1 2029, also 1 year late — consistent pattern of post-boom completion undermines the 기술선도 preemption rationale
